stories.title: Coeur d’Alene Tribe saves with solar-powered rec center

stories.extended_summary: On the Coeur d'Alene Reservation in Idaho, kids swim and play at the Marimn Health Coeur Center, a 32,000-square-foot rec center powered partly by the sun. Rooftop solar panels installed two years ago were expected to save $2,500 a year—but with rising utility costs, the tribe is now saving about four times that. Environmental programs manager Laura Laumatia says the project is about more than money: it's about energy sovereignty. Historically, tribes have had little say in utility development, and four different utilities serve the reservation with no tribal representation. This solar step gives the Coeur d'Alene more control over its own power.
